science.title: Associations between adaptive perfectionism-related orderliness and academic engagement: parallel and ordered indirect associations through self-control and meaning in life
science.description: Academic engagement is a central indicator of students’ learning adaptation and developmental potential, yet the psychological processes underlying the association between adaptive perfectionism-related orderliness and engagement remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on Conservation of Resources theory and Self-Determination Theory, this study examined the associations among adaptive perfectionism-related orderliness, self-control, meaning in life, and academic engagement. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 1083 Chinese university students recruited through convenience sampling. Structural equation modeling and bias-corrected bootstrapping were used to examine parallel and ordered indirect associations. Adaptive perfectionism-related orderliness was positively associated with academic engagement. Significant indirect associations were observed through self-control and meaning in life separately, together with a significant ordered indirect association involving both variables. These findings suggest that adaptive perfectionism-related orderliness is associated with academic engagement partly through self-regulatory and meaning-related psychological resources. The study extends prior work by integrating these resources within a single multiple-mediator model.

science.title: A membrane-active cationic supramolecule to treat both fungal and bacterial keratitis
science.description: Rising antimicrobial resistance (AMR) underscores the urgent need for new antimicrobial strategies. We report here a membrane-active cationic supramolecule and its strong therapeutic efficacy against both fungal and bacterial keratitis in animal models. The lead Y8 design displayed broad-spectrum activity against various fungal pathogens, with low-µM MIC90, rapid action kinetics, and resistance evasion. Mechanistically, it disrupts the fungal cytoplasmic membrane and interacts with the cell wall glucan. Y8 is ocular compatible and, more importantly, shows higher/comparable efficacy to voriconazole, natamycin and amphotericin B in treating Candida, Fusarium and Aspergillus keratitis in mice or rabbits, respectively. It further displays strong activity against pathogenic bacteria, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), with markedly better treatment outcomes than vancomycin in a mouse MRSA keratitis model. Overall, here we demonstrate a safe, potent, and cross-kingdom antimicrobial strategy, which may potentially contribute to the frontline infection management and AMR crisis mitigation. In this work, authors report a membrane-active cationic supramolecule, Y8, with potent cross-kingdom activity against vision-threatening fungal and bacterial keratitis. It is ocular-compatible and outperforms or matches standard therapies in animal models.

science.title: Green synthesis of Colocasia esculenta-mediated nickel ferrite nanoparticles: dual applications in photocatalytic wastewater treatment and antifungal activity
science.description: Colocasia esculenta leaf extract was employed as a plant-derived synthesis aid for the preparation of nickel ferrite (NiFe2O4) nanoparticles, which were evaluated for visible-light methylene blue (MB) degradation and antifungal activity against Candida albicans. X-ray diffraction confirmed the cubic spinel phase with an average crystallite size of approximately 20 nm, whereas SEM showed secondary particles/agglomerates in the range of 80–150 nm. UV–visible/Tauc analysis gave an optical band gap of 1.57 eV. Under the optimized photocatalytic conditions investigated in this study (5 ppm MB, 50 mg catalyst and pH 11), the degradation efficiency reached approximately 99%, and the catalyst retained high activity over four reuse cycles. In the biological assays, the nanoparticle formulation produced an inhibition zone of 20.00 ± 0.20 mm against C. albicans, with MIC and MFC values of 4 and 32 µg mL−1, respectively. Biofilm biomass and filamentation were reduced by approximately 76% and 74%, respectively. These results demonstrate that NiFe2O4 prepared using C. esculenta can serve as a multifunctional material for photocatalytic wastewater treatment and in vitro antifungal applications.
